messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on the Token Scope Cartography idea I posted in the RFC — want to sketch a rollout plan here and call out tradeoffs. TL;DR: map every key type to a clear org/project/service axis, add a short-lived projection for service tokens, and run staged canaries + audit telemetry.

maria: Why — we've seen user confusion and silent fallbacks when tokens lack intended scope metadata. That increases blast radius and makes routing hard for infra (esp. Dedicated/Private modes). We need clearer semantics before bigger migrations (model routing, quota isolation).

maria: Proposal (high level):
1) Discovery: run a bulk scan to cartograph existing tokens (api keys, svc keys, operator tokens) and produce a CSV with columns: token_id, holder_type, inferred_org, inferred_project, service_hint, last_seen, uses_count.
2) Schema: consolidate scope encoding to 3 canonical dimensions: org, project (optional), principal (user/service). Token type remains: user, svc, operator.
3) Short-lived projection: for service-to-service calls introduce ephemeral projection tokens minted by a broker with lifetime 1h by default.
4) Rollout: opt-in canary routes -> shadow enforcement -> gradual cutoff with fallback gate.
5) Telemetry + audits: per-token resolution path logged; add regression alerts when >1% requests hit fallback routing in a route/week.

maria: Example encoded hint (not auth header):
```
svc:svc-123:org:org-45:proj:proj-9:scope:write
user:user-987:org:org-45:scope:read
```
These are metadata strings attached to tokens in the inventory; not necessarily the raw token form.

samir: +1 for cartography but worried about naive mapping. Many tokens are reused across multiple projects (integration tests, infra scripts). How do we avoid accidental lockout?
samir: suggestion: add "shared" flag and automated migration mode that preserves dual-binding for 2 weeks before enforcing.

maria: good call — migration modes: 
- observe-only (no enforcement)
- soft-enforce (reject if mismatch but allow with logged override)
- hard-enforce (reject)
We'll default to observe-only for 30d after discovery, then soft-enforce 14d, then hard-enforce by opt-in per org.

jess: on the short-lived service tokens: also recommend default audience claim for service tokens so they can't be used with unrelated endpoints. That plus ttl avoids blast radius. Also rotate broker signing keys every 7d?
jess: note: ops burden higher if rotation too frequent; propose 7d for high-risk orgs, 30d global default.

jeff: telemetry question — what fields do we emit? We should include resolved_org, resolved_project, resolution_path (inferred|explicit|brokered), and authz_policy_version. Without these, post-mortems will be painful. Also we need a dashboard for routes hitting fallback.

maria: agree. We'll add a telemetry envelope. Also: backlog item to add per-route rejection reasons to the Console (so teams can debug why a token was rejected/mapped).

samir: performance tradeoff: resolution at ingress adds ~0.5ms p50 in current runtime if we do a lookup per-request. Can we cache resolution for token fingerprint + TTL? If caching, need eviction and consistency when tokens are rotated.

maria: yes, propose a two-tier cache: local (in-process) 1s TTL for hot paths + global shared cache (redis) 60s TTL for cross-worker consistency. Cache invalidation triggered on key rotation webhook.

jess: ops note: the token broker must support on-demand audit proof (signatures) to satisfy compliance audits. Keep an exportable history of minted projections.

devops-bot: deploybot: branch token-scope-cartography/initial pushed to infra-staging, runbook added: https://go/redwood/runbooks/token-cartography (staging deploy in 5m)

maria: timeline draft:
- Week 0-2: discovery + CSV + per-org smoke tests (observe-only)
- Week 3-4: shadow enforcement + telemetry dashboards
- Week 5-6: opt-in soft-enforce for early adopters + broker for service tokens in staging
- Week 7-8: public soft-enforce + further monitoring
- Week 9+: per-org cutover plan (hard-enforce optional)

maria: open questions we should track here: 
- migration UX for 3rd party integrators (webhooks, SDKs)
- default TTL for projection tokens (1h vs 4h)
- operator tokens: maintain as long-lived but require bound org tag?
- rollbacks: safe rollback plan if we see >2% request failure in 24h after soft-enforce

samir: agree on the rollback rule. Also request a quick script to surface top 50 tokens by request volume so teams can pre-notify owners.

jeff: also add quota cost signals — some tokens belong to infra pipelines with high QPS; hard-enforce must allow policy exceptions for high-throughput infra.

jess: implementation owners? I can take the broker + rotation bits. Maria will own discovery + landing CSV. Samir and infra team handle cache + ingress hooks. Jeff will own telemetry/dashboarding.

maria: thanks — I'll open the migration checklist RFC PR with the phases and attach the discovery script. Posting the CSV schema in the PR. Can everyone ack on this thread so I can start scheduling the discovery run?

samir: ack
jess: ack
jeff: ack
